**Finding submitted: deviation (TRANSITION).**

**What I checked**
- Article 12 in full (term, breach, at-will, insolvency, reversion, terminated territory, survival, sell-off).
- Section 9.7/9.8 (return of Confidential Information), Section 3.8.5–3.8.6 (records, survives), Sections 3.5/4.5.2–4.5.3 (IND transition and Manufacturing Technology Transfer — all in-Term, not post-termination).

**Why it fails the fallback**
- Exit mechanics run outbound: 12.6.1(c) and 12.7.2–12.7.8 make *us* transfer or destroy data, regulatory materials and know-how; nothing requires Harpoon to give post-termination transition assistance or return our data on a defined timeline.
- Section 9.7 is the only data-return mechanic — request-based, "as soon as reasonably practicable," no machine-readable format, and its one-archival-copy carve-out does not reach the separate destruction election in 12.6.1(c).
- 12.6.1(c) lets Harpoon elect immediate destruction of data we generated with no carve-out for records required by Applicable Law (including our own retention duty under 3.8.5), pharmacovigilance or litigation holds — squarely the playbook's walk-away scenario.
- 12.10.2 gives a commercial sell-off period only; no data or transition support.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level)**
1. 12.6.1(c): 30-day, machine-readable transfer plus a retention carve-out for legally required, pharmacovigilance, litigation and archival copies.
2. New 12.6.6 "Wind-Down Support": up to six months' transition assistance at our cost, return of our data within 30 days in machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification.

Fallback offered in the comment: 90 days of assistance with a 30-day export.
